ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, D is the midpoint of AB, $AC=5$, and $BC=12$. What is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In right triangle $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=5$, $BC=12$,\\
$\therefore AB= \sqrt{AC^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}=13$,\\
$\because D$ is the midpoint of $AB$,\\
$\therefore AD=BD$,\\
$\therefore CD= \frac{1}{2} AB=\boxed{6.5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC with A at the upper left, C at the lower left, and B at the lower right. Segment AC is vertical and segment CB is horizontal, forming a right angle at C. Point D lies on the slanted side AB, and segment CD is drawn from C to D. Reasoning: From the text, AC = 5, BC = 12, angle ACB = 90°, and D is the midpoint of AB. Since ABC is a right triangle with legs AC and BC, the hypotenuse is AB = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = sqrt(169) = 13. In a right triangle, the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices, so CD equals half of AB. Therefore CD = 13/2 = 6.5.
